name: Netherlands: check of forms and supplied documents

common.check: Trial title and EU trial number (if assigned) match the protocol and CTIS.
Every field the assistant answers is answered; fields that belong to the site, investigator, institution or insurer are left empty, not invented.
No drafting instruction remains (yellow [INSERT/IF/OTHERWISE/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); template boilerplate marked as a note is deleted.

Language matches requirements.json language_rules; signature only where the Dutch rule for that document requires it (VGO front sheet signed; K, L and M not signed at submission; GDPR statement may be unsigned).
CTIS title and upload location follow the naming guide and requirements.json.
The current mandatory national template is used where the Netherlands requires one (VGO, P1, R1), not a sponsor or generic EU substitute.

NL-B1-COVER.check: Current European cover-letter template, in the CTIS Form section, unsigned.
States the MREC proposed to assess the trial in the Netherlands.
Combined study with a medical device or IVD identified, with the relevant EU CT and NL numbers, shared documents and the coordinated Dutch process.
Gives the reason why the complete IVO exceeds 4,000 words.
Version dates of the documents listed match the document list and the documents.

NL-FEE-INVOICE.check: Dutch invoice-details template uploaded under Proof of payment of fee; no advance proof of payment.
Invoice details complete and supplied by the sponsor (CCMO invoice payable within 30 days).

NL-GDPR-STATEMENT.check: EU GDPR compliance statement uploaded in the CTIS Form section, not in Part II R.
Sponsor details match the CTIS application; name and role of the responsible person come from the sponsor.
The Dutch Part II R1 form (NL-R1) is also present; the two are not confused.

NL-K1.check: Uses the harmonised European Recruitment and Informed Consent Procedure template v2.0, not the superseded version.

The yes/no answers for incapacitated adults, minors, impartial witness and emergency match the project's populations and study facts; each 'yes' section is completed, each 'no' section gives the not-applicable answer.
Covers the first act of recruitment, identification and approach, access to identifiable records, consent setting and reflection time.

Member State fields carry the Dutch rules: only Dutch documents assessed; IVO for 16 or older; signatures of participant and researcher or authorised interviewer; explicit consent for medical-record access; translation and translation-certificate procedure where non-Dutch speakers are planned.
Adults lacking capacity: 'no, unless' conditions, capacity assessment, Dutch representative order, adapted participant information, objection respected, own re-consent on regaining capacity.
Minors: under-12 and 12-15 rules, both parents with parental authority or the guardian, resistance statement and handling, re-consent at 12, no new consent solely at 16.
Impartial witness (section 5): only for inability to write, sign or read; selection and independence; alternative recording method.

Emergency (section 6): every Article 35 condition, CCMO deferred-consent memorandum, earliest approach of representative and participant, refusal, data retention, death before consent, mixed-population justification.
Recruitment routes and first act of recruitment match the recruitment material (K2) and the protocol, which describes every consent pathway.

NL-M1.check: One dated CV per principal investigator and Dutch site, no more than two years old.
Prefer unsigned (CCMO treats signatures as personal data); official CV template used or an equivalent CV.
Only trial fields prepared by the assistant; personal content from the investigator; site registered in CTIS only once CV, DoI and signed VGO are complete.

NL-M2-DOI.check: One separate dated declaration per principal investigator and Dutch site on the official European declaration-of-interest template.
No handwritten signature required; interests answered by the investigator.

NL-N1.check: Official Dutch Site Suitability Declaration (VGO) used for every Dutch site, including a single-centre trial; not the generic EU site-suitability form.
Signed front sheet uploaded; signed by the executive board or management of the institution (validated digital signature accepted).
Dutch or English version as chosen by the institution; site details consistent with the CTIS site record, M1 and M2.
Clinical Trial Agreement not uploaded in CTIS.

NL-O1.check: WMO participant-insurance certificate compliant with the Medical Research (Human Subjects) Compulsory Insurance Decree 2015, covering the whole trial.
For a qualifying low-intervention trial: a reasoned exemption request instead of presenting the exemption as automatic.
Insurer, policy details, claims contact and coverage match the information sheet and its insurance appendix (or the exemption wording).

NL-O2.check: Liability cover or another adequate financial guarantee is in place for the sponsor or executing party, also where participant insurance is exempt (except the statutory government exception).
Separate proof uploaded under Proof of insurance cover or indemnification.

NL-P1.check: National Dutch P1 template used (not the generic EU compensation template).
Covers funding, payments to the investigator or site, participant compensation, reimbursements, other arrangements, and the Dutch review points on publication and early termination.
Healthy-volunteer compensation described transparently and proportionate to time and burden.
Amounts, methods and conditions identical in P1, the IVO and every participant document.

NL-R1.check: Official Dutch R1 national data-protection form (16 January 2026) uploaded under Compliance with national requirements on data protection.
Separate from the GDPR statement in the CTIS Form section; both present.
Data flows, controllers, coding, retention, transfers and contacts match the participant documents and S1.

NL-S1.check: Official biological-samples template (EudraLex-aligned Dutch form) completed; new and archive sample sections match the protocol and sample plan.
Collection, storage, transfer, analysis, destruction and future use described and consistent with the protocol, participant information and R1.
Future use: separate optional choice, data and bodily material distinguished, fixed storage period and location, coded samples not called anonymous, withdrawal and destruction rules.
Section 5 (f03) carries the Dutch national points.
